Title: Fed Dot Plot Highlights Wide Disparity Of Views On Future Rate Cuts

Summary: 
At its September 17 meeting, the Federal Reserve lowered the federal‑funds rate by 25 basis points, a move that passed with an 11‑to‑1 vote, showing a rare consensus in a highly partisan climate.  However, the Fed’s quarterly dot plot reveals a sharp division among its 19 members about future cuts.  In the latest third‑quarter plot, nine participants expect only one more cut this year, while ten foresee two cuts, and just one member projects no cuts.  One official even projected a 1.25‑percentage‑point cut by the end of 2025.  Earlier in the year, March’s plot had 13 members forecasting one or two cuts and only four predicting no change; by June the split widened, with eight anticipating two cuts and seven expecting no change.  The dot plot’s anonymity means the identities of the predictions are unknown, but the pattern suggests the Fed may be leaning toward a more neutral or even accommodative stance for the rest of 2025.

Published date: September 18 2025, 02:48

Title: Fed se inclina por dos recortes más a su tasas de interés antes de fin de año, revelan minutas | El Universal

Summary: 
According to the minutes from the Federal Reserve's September meeting, released on October 8, 2025, the majority of Federal Reserve officials favor two additional interest rate cuts before the end of the year, though with caution due to inflation risks. Eleven of the 12 voting members supported a 0.25 percentage point reduction, lowering the federal funds rate to a range of 4.0% to 4.25%, marking the first rate cut of the year. The sole dissenting vote came from Governor Stephen Miran, a Trump-appointed member of the Board of Governors, who has previously pressured Chair Jerome Powell to accelerate rate reductions. The minutes reveal internal division: while most believe further cuts are necessary to sustain economic growth and prevent rising unemployment, others warn that cutting rates too quickly could reignite inflation, which remains above the Fed’s 2% target. The minutes indicate uncertainty about the total number of cuts this year—either two or three, including the September reduction—and emphasize that future decisions will depend on key indicators such as employment and inflation data. Analysts note that Fed decisions directly impact mortgages, personal and business loans, and financial markets, with markets already pricing in cautious action. The overall tone of the minutes reflects a careful balance between stimulating the economy and maintaining credibility in the fight against inflation.

Published date: October 08 2025, 21:48

Title: Fed's Kashkari sees two more rate cuts in 2025. Here's why.

Summary: 
Minneapolis Fed President Neil Kashkari, in a new essay, says he is more concerned about the jobs market than sticky inflation. He now expects three rate cuts in 2025, up from two in June. He notes the risk of a sharp increase in unemployment warrants action to support the labor market, but says the Fed is not on a preset course for cuts. If the labor market strengthens, the Fed could pause or even raise rates. On inflation, he expects uncertainty around tariffs but does not foresee inflation rising above 3%, and says he is monitoring inflation expectations and the threat to central bank independence.

Title: Minutas de la Fed sugieren que las tasas de interés seguirán bajando - Alto Nivel

Summary: 
The Federal Reserve's minutes from its latest meeting, released on October 8, 2025, indicate that officials anticipate at least two additional interest rate cuts in 2025, with some considering a third, while a minority expects no further reductions. This outlook reflects concerns over a weakening labor market and the need to balance persistent inflation. The Fed emphasized that monetary policy is not on a predetermined path, and future decisions will depend on incoming data on growth, employment, inflation, and emerging economic risks. Chairman Jerome Powell stated the strategy aims to avoid both excessive job market deterioration and overly high inflation, noting there is 'no risk-free path.' Since the start of 2025, the U.S. dollar (DXY index) has weakened by 8.8%. The Fed faces limited data availability due to an ongoing federal government shutdown, now in its eighth day, which delayed key reports such as the September employment data. Historically, such shutdowns have led the Fed to adopt a more dovish stance, as noted by The Kobeissi Letter. The next monetary policy meeting is scheduled for October 28–29, 2025, when officials will reassess economic data. According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, 92.5% of the market expects a 25-basis-point rate cut at the next meeting. Additionally, 77.6% of the market anticipates rates will end the year in a range of 3.5%–3.75%, representing a 50-basis-point reduction from the current level, with cumulative cuts of 75 basis points in 2025. Inflation remains above target, with headline inflation estimated at 2.7% and core inflation at 2.9% in August. Officials warned that recent tariff hikes and immigration restrictions could impact both prices and job creation, while credit conditions remain relatively stable for businesses and consumers. The Fed plans to continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and mortgage-backed debt while maintaining flexibility to adjust policy as the economy evolves.

Published date: October 08 2025, 19:53

URL: https://www.altonivel.com.mx/minutas-de-la-fed-sugieren-que-las-tasas-de-interes-seguiran-bajando/
Source: Alto Nivel
Classification: Finance
Sentiment: neutral
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: North America

Title: Fed makes first rate cut of 2025 and signals more to come

Summary: 
The Federal Reserve announced its first rate cut of 2025, lowering the policy rate by a quarter point and signalling that two additional cuts are likely later in the year, which would bring the target range to 3.5%–3.75% by year‑end.  The FOMC’s dot plot shows that nearly all officials expect easing, with most forecasting three cuts, some two, and one even projecting six cuts.  The Fed also revised its economic outlook, raising its GDP growth forecast while noting a potential rise in the unemployment rate to 4.5% by year‑end and an increase in core PCE inflation, suggesting a more stagflationary environment.  These developments indicate that the Fed is prepared to lower rates more consistently even in the face of sticky inflation.

Published date: September 17 2025, 21:50

URL: https://ca.news.yahoo.com/fed-makes-first-rate-cut-215055491.html
Source: Yahoo

Sentiment: neutral
Reporting voice: Objective

Citation key: [10]
Title: Fed governor maintains outlook for three interest cuts in 2025

Summary: 
Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman reiterated her call for three interest rate cuts in 2025, citing signs of fragility in labor market conditions and a shift in economic conditions. Bowman, who dissented from the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged in July, explained that inflation has moved closer to the target and the labor market remains near full employment. She noted that the July jobs report was weaker than expected and that the labor market data have become increasingly difficult to interpret. Bowman emphasized that monetary policy isn't on a predetermined path and could evolve as economic conditions change. She continues to project three interest rate cuts before the end of 2025, implying three 25-basis-point cuts at upcoming FOMC meetings.

Published date: August 11 2025, 16:23

URL: https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/fed-governor-maintains-outlook-three-interest-cuts-2025
Source: Fox Business
